drhp.business: The Company runs three distinct divisions. The Agency Division markets and sells textile spinning machinery to spinning mills; the Textile (Yarn) Division manufactures cotton yarn, relying on high-quality imported cotton to hold yarn quality consistent because locally available cotton was not found fully suitable for the desired product standards; and the Engineering Division manufactures gears/gearboxes, including OEM business. Yarn and gears are sold domestically and exported directly, with merchant exports forming part of the yarn export book.

risks.note: Management attributes the Agency Division's only marginal topline and bottom-line growth to 'the continued slowdown in the textile industry', with subdued business sentiment. The Agency division sells spinning machinery and the Textile division sells yarn, so a single industry downturn hits most of the Company's revenue base.
risks.risk: Dependence on the textile cycle - a slowdown in the textile industry directly suppresses two of the three divisions

risks.note: 'Business sentiment remained subdued as customers adopted a cautious approach towards capital expenditure and new machinery investments, resulting in slower order conversions.' The Agency division's revenue depends on spinning mills committing to new machinery, so a capex pause converts directly into deferred orders; investment continued only 'selectively' and 'at a gradual pace'.
risks.risk: Customer capital-expenditure deferral slows order conversion

risks.note: Management flags 'a temporary impact of tariff rate revisions' on the Agency division and states that 'during the year, changes in tariff rates had a temporary impact on margins, though the situation subsequently stabilized' in the Textile division. Margins are therefore exposed to a policy variable outside the Company's control.
risks.risk: Tariff rate revisions / import-export policy changes hit margins

risks.note: 'The division continued to rely on high-quality imported cotton to ensure consistency in yarn quality ... as the quality of locally available cotton was not found to be fully suitable for the desired product standards.' Cost competitiveness was supported by 'the Government's extension of customs duty exemption on imported cotton up to December 2025' - an input-cost benefit with a stated end-date, and a structural dependence on imported raw material even when domestic cotton prices are stable.
risks.risk: Reliance on imported cotton, with the supporting customs duty exemption dated

risks.note: The Directors cite 'the prevailing global geopolitical uncertainties and war-related developments' as continuing to cast a cautious outlook on the industry, and note the 'impact of geopolitical uncertainties and tariff rate changes on global trade' against which direct exports grew. Yarn exports (including merchant exports) and Gears division exports are a material part of the book.
risks.risk: Geopolitical uncertainty and war-related developments weighing on global trade and the export book

risks.note: The Company both earns foreign exchange (Rs. 4257.03 Lakhs) and incurs foreign exchange outgo, dominated by raw material imports (Rs. 2069.49 Lakhs of a Rs. 2259.47 Lakhs total). Currency and import-cost movements therefore feed into yarn conversion economics as well as export realisations.
risks.risk: Foreign-currency exposure on both sides of the trade - export earnings against imported raw material

risks.note: The Directors' Report technology-absorption disclosure returns blank entries for efforts towards technology absorption, benefits derived (product improvement, cost reduction, import substitution) and expenditure on research and development, leaving the businesses reliant on operating efficiency rather than proprietary product development for differentiation.
risks.risk: Low technology-absorption and R&D intensity disclosed
